rounds.proof_sketch: Host computes num_blocks=ceil(total/256). Mutant kernel uses elements_per_block=257, so block B covers [257*B, 257*(B+1)-1]. Block B ends at 257*B+256, block B+1 starts at 257*B+257 - consecutive, no gaps. Total coverage = num_blocks*257 >= (total/256)*257 > total, so all elements covered. Guard condition prevents OOB. Each element computed exactly once with identical formula.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes elements_per_block from 256 to 257 inside the kernel only, while the host code still uses 256 to compute num_blocks. This creates a different block-to-element mapping: mutant blocks process slightly more elements each. However, since (1) there are no gaps between consecutive blocks (257B+256 and 257(B+1) are adjacent), (2) the total coverage num_blocks×257 exceeds total_output_elements, and (3) the guard condition prevents out-of-bounds processing, every output element is computed exactly once with the same averaging formula. The only difference is which GPU thread performs each computation, which doesn't affect the result.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation only affects internal work distribution across CUDA blocks without changing which elements are computed or their values. Mathematical analysis proves complete coverage without gaps under all possible total_output_elements values.
rounds.recommendations: For mutations affecting block/thread work distribution constants, mutation testing tools should perform static analysis to verify that: (1) host and kernel use consistent values when they must match, OR (2) the kernel's internal redistribution still guarantees complete coverage. This mutation survives because the loop guard and contiguous block coverage make the internal constant value irrelevant to correctness.
